stem.en: Kabir runs the bench for twice as long. What happens to the ratio of the two gases?

text.en: It stays 2 to 1. Both tubes hold twice as much, and the ratio is fixed by what water is made of.

feedback.en: Twice as long gives twice the oxygen too. Water can only come apart in the ratio it was put together.

text.en: It becomes 1 to 1, because the oxygen catches up.

feedback.en: Oxygen is not slow; each water molecule simply gives two hydrogens and one oxygen, every time, from the first bubble to the last.

text.en: The water runs out and the ratio stops meaning anything.

feedback.en: A bowl of water is billions of billions of molecules. A battery would take weeks to empty it, and the ratio would be 2 to 1 the whole way.

explanation.en: Every water molecule that is split gives the same pieces. Run it longer and you split more molecules, not different ones.
